findings.title: Non-atomic match_count increment causes race condition
findings.body: should_block? reads the record, increments match_count in Ruby, then saves. Under concurrent requests for the same blocked email (e.g. a spam signup burst), multiple processes/threads can read the same match_count value before any save completes, causing lost updates. Should use an atomic SQL update (e.g. update_all with `match_count = match_count + 1`) instead.

findings.title: should_block? mutates state on every validation call, including failed saves/dry runs
findings.body: should_block? is called from EmailValidator.validate_each, which can run multiple times per request (e.g. valid? called twice as in UsersController#create: `user.valid? && SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` then save). This causes match_count to be incremented more than once per actual signup attempt, inflating statistics inaccurately.

findings.title: Exposing full error hash and raw submitted values in JSON response
findings.body: The create action now returns `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` to the client. This leaks server-side validation error structure and echoes back submitted values (including email) in all failure cases, which was not previously exposed. While used by the JS to populate rejectedEmails, this changes the API contract and could leak more information than intended (e.g. internal error keys for other attributes beyond email).

findings.title: Email validator order allows email_domains validation to run even when blocked
findings.body: The new EmailValidator (lib/validators/email_validator.rb) always evaluates email_domains_whitelist/blacklist and only checks BlockedEmail.should_block? when no prior error exists, meaning should_block? (and its side-effecting match_count update) is skipped if the domain whitelist/blacklist already rejects the email. This means blocked-email statistics won't be collected for already-blacklisted domains, which may be surprising/inconsistent with the intent of tracking all block attempts.

findings.title: Missing newline at end of file
findings.body: The file lacks a trailing newline, which is a minor style/lint issue but can cause warnings in some Ruby tooling/CI configured to enforce file-ending newlines.

findings.title: rejectedEmails is a shared singleton array across controller instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([]),` is defined as a literal array on the prototype/mixin level. In Ember/Discourse's object model, if CreateAccountController is reused as a shared instance (typical for Ember controllers), this is fine, but if multiple instances are created this literal array will be shared across all instances since it's evaluated once at class definition. This can cause rejected emails from one modal session to leak into another, so emails rejected in a previous attempt may incorrectly block valid emails in a new session unless the controller object is a true singleton that gets reset elsewhere.
